topic: Will the world's population keep growing indefinitely?

trajectory_record.statement: No true MCTS or evolutionary trajectory was run. The portfolio is a transparent comparison of routes constrained by the frozen Survey handoff; no synthetic evolution history is claimed.

competitive_ideas.name: Projection reconciliation dashboard
competitive_ideas.mechanism: Harmonize published scenario outputs and report differences in peak date and total.
competitive_ideas.rejection_reason: Descriptive reconciliation cannot test component mechanisms or persistence conditions.

competitive_ideas.name: Component-resolved peak persistence atlas
competitive_ideas.mechanism: Generate coherent country-age-sex cohort trajectories from fertility, mortality, and migration ensembles; pre-register a climate-modifier comparison and calculate the posterior probability of post-2100 positive global growth.
competitive_ideas.strength: Directly ties the question to calibrated components, uncertainty propagation, and decision rules.

competitive_ideas.name: Climate-only demographic causal model
competitive_ideas.mechanism: Estimate one global climate coefficient for long-run population change.
competitive_ideas.rejection_reason: The Survey does not support homogeneous causal identification; this violates the frozen uncertainty boundary.

high_risk_ideas.name: Joint demographic-integrated-assessment model
high_risk_ideas.risk: Strong feedback claims between population, economy, emissions, and climate would require evidence and structural assumptions outside the frozen Survey scope.

rejected_ideas.name: One-number answer for the 2100 population
rejected_ideas.reason: Contradicts probabilistic evidence and cannot represent component or structural uncertainty.

rejected_ideas.name: Indefinite-growth proof
rejected_ideas.reason: A finite historical record and finite forecast horizon cannot prove an infinite-horizon population proposition.

selected_primary_idea.title: Component-Resolved Population Peak Persistence Atlas
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Annual country-by-age-by-sex population trajectories and their global aggregate.
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: A jointly calibrated, probabilistic cohort-component ensemble can distinguish post-2100 growth-persistence conditions from earlier-peak conditions and can show whether climate-disruption covariates add predictive value beyond demographic components alone.
selected_primary_idea.proposed_relation: Fertility, survival, and net migration update cohorts; posterior draws are aggregated to a global annual growth process. Climate-disruption covariates can alter component forecasts only when they improve held-out predictive scoring and calibration.
falsification_conditions: The ensemble fails pre-specified holdout calibration or has poorer predictive scores than a simpler baseline.
Component attribution is unstable across reasonable historical cutoffs or aggregation levels.
Climate-modifier models do not improve held-out score or calibration relative to the no-climate model.
The posterior probability of post-2100 positive growth changes mainly with unsupported prior choices.
selected_primary_idea.feasibility_path: Use public WPP country-age-sex series as the core accounting data, pre-register data transformations and withheld years, fit only approved model families, and execute only after independent demographic and data-governance review.
